record.original_question: Study the transformations that preserve random strings and random sequences.

evidence.quote: Study the transformations that preserve random strings and sequences. (C. Calude, H. Jürgensen)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{0,1\}^*$ denote the set of finite binary strings and $\{0,1\}^\omega$ the set of infinite binary sequences. Fix a universal prefix-free Turing machine $U$ and let $K(x)$ denote the prefix-free Kolmogorov complexity of $x \in \{0,1\}^*$. Call a finite string $x$ of length $n$ Chaitin/Kolmogorov random (with parameter $c$) if $K(x) \geq n - c$, and call an infinite sequence $\alpha \in \{0,1\}^\omega$ Martin-Löf random if it is not contained in any effectively presented null $G_\delta$ set (equivalently, if there is a constant $c$ such that $K(\alpha\restriction n) \geq n - c$ for all $n$).

A function $T: \{0,1\}^* \to \{0,1\}^*$ is said to preserve randomness of strings if there exists a constant $c_T$ such that whenever $x$ is Kolmogorov random, $T(x)$ is Kolmogorov random with parameter $c_T$. A function $F: \{0,1\}^\omega \to \{0,1\}^\omega$ is said to preserve randomness of sequences if $F(\alpha)$ is Martin-Löf random whenever $\alpha$ is Martin-Löf random.

Characterize, as completely as possible, the class of computable transformations $T$ on finite binary strings that preserve Kolmogorov randomness, and the class of computable (or Turing-reducibility–induced) transformations $F$ on infinite binary sequences that preserve Martin-Löf randomness. In particular, give necessary and sufficient conditions on such transformations, and identify natural operations (e.g., changes of base for representations of real numbers, finite-state transductions, computable permutations) that lie in these classes.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Calude and Jürgensen (1994) showed that Martin-Löf randomness is invariant under change of positional base for representations of reals, and there is a substantial body of subsequent work on randomness preservation under computable measure-preserving maps, finite-state transducers, and Turing functionals (e.g., results of Bienvenu, Merkle, Shen and others). However, a complete characterization of all randomness-preserving transformations on strings and sequences as posed by Calude and Jürgensen remains open in full generality.

status_evidence.title: Randomness as an invariant for number representations
status_evidence.snippet: Calude and Jürgensen show that the usual positional representations of a real number are either random (Martin-Löf) for all bases or for none.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: randomness is invariant under change of base.

status_evidence.title: Information and Randomness: An Algorithmic Perspective
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph by Calude discussing randomness-preserving transformations as part of algorithmic information theory.
status_evidence.claim: Topic discussed but no complete characterization given.
